title: Unit Event — Knowing the Unseen — Episode6 The Surrounding Night

meta.Event Outline: Ena debates whether she should aim for art school post-graduation. With this inner turmoil comes restlessness, which begins to affect her art. Mr. Yukihira notices that she's struggling, and after she divulges the cause, he invites her to take part in an excursion.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (The painting of this peony...)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (It feels less dark compared to the others.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (The previous piece had really dark shadows. With paint everywhere and the canvas on the ground... It was like nothing mattered anymore to him...)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (But this one's a little different...)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (A moonbeam is illuminating this peony. As though it's giving it life.)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (But the dark areas around it...)

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (It looks quite messy, despite the peony itself being painted carefully.)

rows.Speaker: Rin
rows.Line:
<There's something off about this painting...
The flower's really pretty, but everything else is so dark.>

rows.Speaker: Len
rows.Line: <Yeah, it's interesting in that sense...>

rows.Speaker: Len
rows.Line: <What do you think was going through your dad's mind when he painted this, Ena...?>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I don't know...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: But unlike those other paintings we just saw, this one involves a source of light...

rows.Speaker: Len
rows.Line: <Light...>

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Yeah. It's hard to ignore the shadows and darkness, but he seemed to put a lot of effort into this beam of light...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: But if his goal was to paint something about light, I feel that he would've done something different...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: (What was going through his mind when he painted this...?)

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: Shinonome.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Oh...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
How are things going?
What do you feel when you see this painting...?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Pain of some kind.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: Pain?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Yes...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: This peony's pretty, but everything else around it feels like it was painted in a frenzy...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: No, wait... But...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
Yes...?
Just try to say what comes to mind.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: O-Okay... Umm...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I noticed something after seeing all his paintings up to this period...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: For some reason, his works from around this time all seem to evoke pain and suffering...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line:
But he feels that he has to keep drawing.
That's sort of what I got out of them...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: And yet...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: This painting... In the midst of the pain, there's also...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: A sense of hope or something similar... I think that's what it's trying to express...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: I see. That's what you felt when you saw this?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Huh...?

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: There was a time when he struggled to overcome a massive creative block.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: I still to this day vividly remember the state he was in.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: He'd finally begun his journey as a painter, but no one seemed interested in looking at his art, let alone understand it.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: He drew and drew as much as he could. He was so desperate.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: I even heard that he was struggling to make ends meet. Things got so hard that his wife had to support him and put food on the table...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: Then, one day, she gave birth to a baby girl.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: What...?

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: That was when he began asking himself...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
“Can I keep going on like this?”
“Should I give up on being an artist?”

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
He decided to do one last painting.
A piece called “A Peony Blooming in the Night”.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: He was ready to quit...?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: You're joking, right? I mean...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
Yes, but...
As you know, he didn't end up quitting.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: I don't fully understand the pain he felt or how he figured out what he needed to do.

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: However...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: I do know that he decided to fully commit himself to his art.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Fully commit...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
Now then, the exhibit's about to open.
Why don't we end our lesson here?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: O-Oh, okay...

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Um, Mr. Yukihira...?

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line: Yes?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Would it be okay if I stayed a little while longer...?

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: I want to take another look at the artwork...

rows.Speaker: Yukihira
rows.Line:
I don't mind.
But I'll be excusing myself here.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Okay.

rows.Speaker: Ena
rows.Line: Thank you very much.
